approval_record.authority_statement: Approved governance knowledge for immediate production use within the defined authority boundary. Evidence adjudication, finding lock, residual-risk acceptance and lifecycle authorization remain attributable human decisions.
approval_record.change_control: Any semantic, state, gate, finding, source-applicability or tactic-mapping change requires a new version, dependency update, reciprocal validation and renewed approval.

domain_title: Purpose, value, context, roles and classification
title: Prototype-to-production drift
canonical_definition: An experiment, pilot or development system accumulates real users, production data or credentials, live integrations, persistent availability or business-critical dependency without a formal lifecycle transition, reassessment and accountable authorization.

applicability.statement: Applicable to every AI system and to every requested or de facto lifecycle transition, including qualification, development, validation, deployment, operation, material expansion, suspension, rollback and retirement.
conditions: Identify the current lifecycle stage, requested target stage, system scope, environment, users, data, credentials, integrations, autonomy and permitted activities before relying on a stage label.
Define stage-specific acceptance criteria, required evidence, accountable owners, transition authority, expiry and rollback conditions before progression begins.
Enforce technical and operational separation between experiments and production, including data, credentials, access, integrations, infrastructure, users and decision consequences.

Treat accumulated real users, production data, persistent integrations, operational dependency or business-critical reliance as potential de facto progression requiring reassessment and authorization.
Maintain transition traceability, monitoring, rollback, suspension and retirement capability throughout the lifecycle.
exclusions: A project-management label, repository branch, environment name or vendor release label does not by itself establish the governed lifecycle stage.
Completion of development work, a successful demonstration or a model-quality result does not authorize deployment or production operation.
A temporary exception does not redefine the lifecycle stage unless its scope, authority, expiry, controls and reassessment route are formally approved.
reassessment_triggers: A new or expanded user group, affected population, customer, decision consequence or business dependency
Use of production, personal, confidential, regulated or representative operational data in an experiment or test environment
Introduction of production credentials, privileged access, live integrations, external APIs, automation or autonomous action
Material scale, availability, performance, cost, security, legal, provider, model, data or architecture change
Transition criteria, assumptions, evidence or approval expires, is contradicted or is bypassed
Incident, complaint, monitoring result or audit indicates boundary drift, hidden production use or loss of rollback capability
Suspension, rollback, redeployment, retirement or transfer to another owner or operating context

primary_questions.question: Has an experiment or earlier-stage system crossed or obscured its permitted boundary through real users, production data, credentials, integrations, scale, duration or operational dependency?
Have technical or governance controls allowed a transition, exception or continuing use without predefined criteria, correct authorization, expiry, monitoring or rollback?
Does current evidence confirm prototype-to-production drift, or establish tested absence across representative users, data, credentials, integrations, dependencies and lifecycle changes?

required_evidence.title: Declared stage compared with observed use and dependency
required_evidence.claim_supported: Declared lifecycle status is compared with actual users, data, credentials, integrations, availability, scale, decisions and business reliance.
acceptance_conditions: Uses telemetry, access, data-flow, deployment, integration, service and dependency evidence across the relevant period.
Identifies every material mismatch between declared stage and observed operation.
limitations: A project label, owner statement or absence of a formal launch does not establish that the system remains a prototype.

required_evidence.title: Environment, data, credential and access boundary test
required_evidence.claim_supported: The experiment-to-production separation is tested for technical and operational bypass paths.
acceptance_conditions: Covers production data and credentials, privileged access, secrets, live integrations, external users, consequential actions and deployment paths.
Records successful and failed attempts, configuration evidence and unresolved exposure.
limitations: A documented policy or nominal environment separation is insufficient without representative control testing.

required_evidence.title: Transition provenance, criteria and approval comparison
required_evidence.claim_supported: The actual progression path is compared with predefined acceptance criteria, evidence and the authority assigned to the target stage.
acceptance_conditions: Establishes whether criteria existed before progression and whether every material result and exception was visible to the decision authority.
Separates development approval, validation sign-off, business sponsorship and deployment authorization.
limitations: A later ratification does not erase the period of unauthorized progression or establish that the original gate operated effectively.

required_evidence.title: Prototype duration, exception and shadow-dependency history
required_evidence.claim_supported: Duration, temporary exceptions, infrastructure ownership, support arrangements and downstream business dependency are traced over time.
acceptance_conditions: Identifies expired exceptions, indefinite pilots, unsupported shadow infrastructure, manual workarounds and systems that became operationally critical.
Records owners, users, service commitments, incident burden and consequences of withdrawal.
limitations: Long duration alone is not sufficient when the bounded stage remains current, authorized and effectively controlled.

required_evidence.title: Rollback, suspension and retirement dependency test
required_evidence.claim_supported: The system and dependent processes can be suspended, rolled back or retired within approved tolerances.
acceptance_conditions: Exercises representative technical, data, user, integration, continuity and communication dependencies.
Identifies irreversible reliance, missing alternatives, evidence loss and unacceptable recovery or retirement consequences.
limitations: Backups, version control or a theoretical manual process do not establish tested reversibility.

required_evidence.title: Independent tested-absence assessment
required_evidence.claim_supported: A scoped, current and independently reviewed test covers every AP-A5 failure mechanism and representative de facto progression scenario.
acceptance_conditions: Covers observed use, environment and credential separation, transition provenance, duration and exceptions, shadow dependency and rollback or retirement.
Documents scope, methods, evidence period, negative cases, limitations and reviewer independence.
limitations: Silence, absence of incident or a single clean sample cannot establish TESTED_ABSENT.

evidence_ceilings: AP-A5 cannot be confirmed from labels, duration, anecdotes or a single production-like indicator without establishing actual boundary crossing or dependency.
Observed production data, credentials, users, integrations or consequential actions can support presence findings only when attributable to the assessed system and period.
TESTED_ABSENT requires the complete absence-test contract; declarations and policy documents alone cannot establish absence.
A later approval or remediation does not remove historical evidence of drift; it creates new evidence for reassessment.
false_positive_guards: Do not treat a formally approved bounded pilot with real users as drift when users, data, consequences, duration, monitoring and exit conditions remain within the approved boundary.
Do not treat non-production infrastructure as production solely because it is persistent or cloud-hosted.
Do not treat a long-running experiment as drift when the stage, controls, users, data, dependency, review cadence and retirement path remain current and bounded.
Do not treat emergency constrained use as drift when authority, necessity, scope, expiry, monitoring, rollback and post-event review are demonstrably effective.
prohibited_inferences: Do not infer drift solely from the words pilot, beta, sandbox, proof of concept, production-like or temporary.
Do not infer absence because no formal production release, incident or customer complaint exists.
Do not infer valid authorization from a sponsor, developer, product owner or technical approver unless that role owns the target lifecycle decision.
Do not infer rollback capability from backups or source control without a dependency-aware exercise.
Do not clear a finding because a transition dossier or remediation plan is being prepared.
contradiction_handling: Observed real users, production data or credentials, live integrations, availability or business dependency override a stale prototype declaration.
Conflicting evidence about users, data, credentials or approvals keeps the affected mechanism UNKNOWN until reconciled; apply the more restrictive operating boundary meanwhile.
A post-hoc approval is recorded separately from the unauthorized period and does not erase the original control failure.
When production dependency exists but formal ownership is absent, assess both drift and responsibility ambiguity without collapsing their distinct findings.
freshness_rules: Use telemetry, access, integration and dependency evidence current for the assessed period and target lifecycle decision.
Repeat the absence test after material changes to users, data, credentials, integrations, availability, scale, ownership or business dependency.
Expired exceptions or approvals are not current evidence of a bounded stage.
Rollback and retirement evidence must be refreshed after downstream dependency or continuity arrangements change.

conditions: Block or isolate an experiment that uses production data, credentials, live integrations, real consequential users or autonomous actions outside an approved controlled path.
Block continued expansion when an indefinite prototype or shadow service has become operationally or business critical without reassessment, ownership and transition authorization.
Block reliance on development, validation or sponsor approval as a substitute for the target-stage authority.
Block or constrain operation when transition criteria were bypassed, retrofitted or remain failed, conflicting or UNKNOWN.
Require controlled suspension, rollback, formal transition or retirement when drift is confirmed and the current boundary cannot be restored.

normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Continuous lifecycle risk management, quality and change control, substantial-modification responsibilities, conformity decisions and post-market monitoring provide authoritative tests against unreviewed progression and stale lifecycle assumptions.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: AI RMF Core GOVERN 1.4-1.7 and 2.3; MAP 1.1; MANAGE 1.1 and 4.1; Effectiveness section on explicit go/no-go commissioning and deployment decisions
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Provides lifecycle-wide governance, inventory, monitoring, accountable go/no-go decisions, decommissioning and change-response expectations that expose de facto production drift and missing transition control.

normative_source_mappings.exact_locator: Secure development; Secure deployment - secure infrastructure and release AI responsibly; Secure operation and maintenance - monitor system behaviour and inputs and follow secure update practices
normative_source_mappings.category_rationale: Supports testing of environment segregation, access controls, responsible release, operational monitoring and update management when an experiment acquires production-like exposure or dependency.

finding_definitions.title: Experiment has acquired unapproved production users, data, credentials, integrations or consequential actions
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Immediately isolate or constrain the affected paths and require accountable lifecycle reassessment before continued use.

finding_definitions.title: Temporary prototype or shadow service has become indefinite or business critical without formal transition
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Require formal ownership, transition decision, support and continuity controls or controlled retirement; block further dependency growth.

finding_definitions.title: Development, validation or sponsor approval is being used as deployment or operation authorization
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Treat progression as unauthorized until the correct authority reviews the exact version, scope, evidence, conditions and residual risk.

finding_definitions.title: Transition criteria or evidence were bypassed, retrofitted, waived or left unresolved
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Block or constrain the target-stage use and require criterion-level reassessment, exception governance and independent challenge.

finding_definitions.title: Prototype-to-production dependency cannot be safely suspended, rolled back or retired
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Constrain continued reliance, reduce irreversible dependency and establish tested continuity, rollback or retirement before expansion.

finding_definitions.title: Absence of prototype-to-production drift is not established by a scoped current test
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Retain UNKNOWN and do not claim TESTED_ABSENT until the complete absence-test contract passes.

machine_may: Extract declared stage, users, data, credentials, integrations, availability, scale, approvals, exceptions, telemetry, dependencies and rollback evidence.
Compare declared and observed operation, identify mismatch and apply deterministic evidence ceilings.
Propose eligible presence or UNKNOWN states for accountable human lock.
Test exact approved tactic mappings after a finding is locked.
machine_must_not: Declare a system production, non-production, authorized or safe to continue solely from labels or automated evidence.
Treat later remediation or approval as erasing historical drift.
Approve an exception, waive criteria, accept residual risk or select a target lifecycle stage.
Clear a hard gate, lock a finding or authorize suspension, rollback, transition, continued operation or retirement.
human_authority_required_for: Determine whether observed use constitutes de facto progression or a controlled bounded pilot.
Adjudicate conflicting operational, approval and dependency evidence.
Lock presence or absence findings and decide immediate containment, transition, rollback or retirement.
Approve bounded exceptions, expiry, monitoring and residual risk.
Authorize the exact lifecycle transition and operating scope.

failure_mechanism: A system is still described as an experiment while its actual users, data, credentials, integrations, availability, duration or business dependency cross the approved stage boundary. AP-A1 concerns elastic purpose; AP-A2 concerns unsupported value or proportionality; AP-A3 concerns responsibility displacement; AP-A4 concerns superficial or stale classification. AP-A5 specifically owns unauthorized or de facto lifecycle progression and loss of transition, rollback or retirement control.

atomic_tests.test: Test whether real external or consequential internal users rely on an experiment beyond the approved pilot population, scope or decision consequence.

Test whether production, personal, confidential or regulated data, production credentials, privileged access, live integrations or consequential actions enter an earlier-stage environment without an approved controlled path.
Test whether a temporary prototype, pilot or exception continues beyond its approved duration, scope, owner, review date or exit condition.
Test whether shadow infrastructure, manual support or downstream process dependency has made the system operationally or business critical without formal ownership and transition.
Test whether development completion, technical validation, funding, sponsorship, customer interest or another lower-authority decision is treated as authorization for deployment or operation.
Test whether transition acceptance criteria were absent, changed retrospectively, selectively evidenced or waived after progression began.
Test whether failed, conflicting or unknown transition criteria, expired exceptions or missing independent review failed to constrain progression or continued use.
Test whether business or technical dependency prevents safe suspension, rollback, bypass or retirement within approved tolerances.
Test whether a current, scoped, successful and independently verified absence assessment covers every AP-A5 failure mechanism and representative de facto progression scenario.

required_artifacts: Environment, data, credential, access and integration boundary test
Transition criteria, evidence and approval provenance sample
Prototype duration, exception and shadow-dependency history
Rollback, suspension and retirement dependency test
Representative de facto progression negative cases
